entries.title: Acts 21:1
segments: When at least we had torn ourselves away, and had set sail, we ran a straight course to Cos, and next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

entries.title: Acts 21:2
segments: And when we had found a ship bound for Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.

entries.title: Acts 21:3
segments: After sighting Cyprus and leaving it on the left hand, we sailed for Syria, and put in at Tyre; for there the ship was to unload her cargo.

entries.title: Acts 21:4
segments: We looked up the local disciples and remained there seven days; and these disciples kept telling Paul, through the Spirit, that he should not set foot in Jerusalem.

entries.title: Acts 21:5
segments: When, however, our time was up, we left and started on our journey; and all of them, with wives and children, were escorting us on our way until we were out of the city; then, kneeling down on the beach, we prayed,

entries.title: Acts 21:6
segments: and said good-bye, and went on board the ship, while they returned home again.

entries.title: Acts 21:7
segments: And when we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we reached Ptolemais, and greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.

entries.title: Acts 21:8
segments: On the morrow we started for Caesarea, where we went into the house of Philip, the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

entries.title: Acts 21:9
segments: Now Philip had four unmarried daughters who prophesied,

entries.title: Acts 21:10
segments: and while we remained there many days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

entries.title: Acts 21:11
segments: He came to us, and taking Paul's girdle, he bound his own feet and hands, saying, "Thus says the Holy Spirit, `so will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the owner of this girdle, and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'"

entries.title: Acts 21:12
segments: As soon as we heard these words, both we and those who were standing near entreated Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

entries.title: Acts 21:13
segments: "What do you mean by thus breaking my heart with your grief?" answered Paul. "For I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem, for the name of the Lord Jesus."

entries.title: Acts 21:14
segments: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, "The will of the Lord be done."

entries.title: Acts 21:15
segments: A few days after this we took up our luggage and went up to Jerusalem.

entries.title: Acts 21:16
segments: And some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us. They led us to the house of Mnason, a Cypriote, a disciple of long standing, with whom we were to lodge.

entries.title: Acts 21:17
segments: At length we reached Jerusalem, and the brothers there received us gladly.

entries.title: Acts 21:18
segments: On the following day we went with Paul to call on James, and all the elders were present.

entries.title: Acts 21:19
segments: After saluting them Paul rehearsed, one by one, the things that God had done among the Gentiles by his ministry.

entries.title: Acts 21:20
segments: And they, when they heard it, glorified God, and said to him: "You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews, of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the Law.

entries.title: Acts 21:21
segments: "Now what they have been told about you, again and again, is that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles, to forsake Moses, and not to circumcise their children, nor to follow the old customs.

entries.title: Acts 21:22
segments: "What then ought to be done? They will certainly hear that you are come.

entries.title: Acts 21:23
segments: "So do this that we tell you.

entries.title: Acts 21:24
segments: "We have four men here under a vow; associate yourself with them, purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses so that they may have their heads shaved; then every one will know that there is no truth in the rumors that they have heard about you; but that you yourself walk orderly obeying the law.

entries.title: Acts 21:25
segments: "As for the Gentile believers, we wrote giving judgment that they should abstain from anything sacrificed to an idol, from blood, from what is strangled, and from fornication."

entries.title: Acts 21:26
segments: Then Paul took the men, and after purifying himself with them next day, went into the temple to declare the fulfilment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.

entries.title: Acts 21:27
segments: But when the seven days were almost over, the Asiatic Jews caught sight of him in the temple, and began to stir up all the crowd, and laid hands on him, shouting:

entries.title: Acts 21:28
segments: "Men of Israel, help! This is the man who goes everywhere preaching to everybody against the people, and the Law, and this place. And he has actually brought Gentiles even into the temple, and has desecrated the holy place."

entries.title: Acts 21:29
segments: (For they had formerly seen Trophimus, the Ephesian, with him in the city, and supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.)

entries.title: Acts 21:30
segments: The whole city was thrown into uproar. The mob surged together, seized Paul, and began to drag him outside the temple. Whereupon the doors were at once shut.

entries.title: Acts 21:31
segments: While they were attempting to kill him, news came to the tribune [commander of the garrison] that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

entries.title: Acts 21:32
segments: At once he took soldiers and centurions, and rushed down upon them. When they saw the tribune and the troops, they left off beating Paul.

entries.title: Acts 21:33
segments: Then the tribune came up and seized him, and ordered that he be bound with two chains. "Who is he?" he began asking, "and what has he done?"

entries.title: Acts 21:34
segments: Some among the crowd kept shouting one thing, some another; and when the tribune could not learn the facts because of the uproar, he ordered Paul into the barracks.

entries.title: Acts 21:35
segments: When was going up the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers, because of the violence of the mob,

entries.title: Acts 21:36
segments: for the whole mass of the people were following him, shouting, "Away with him!"

entries.title: Acts 21:37
segments: Just as he was about to be taken into the barracks, Paul said to the tribune, "May I speak to you?"

entries.title: Acts 21:38
segments: "Do you know Greek?" said the tribune; "Are you not, then, the Egyptian who in days gone by stirred up to sedition, and let into the wilderness the four thousand cutthroats?"

entries.title: Acts 21:39
segments: "I am a Jew," answered Paul, "a native of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city. And I pray you, give me permission to speak to the people."
